lines: That clock is set off the halt every morning at six.
Before the line this village was eleven minutes behind the capital and nobody knew.
Now we are all on the same minute. I could not tell you what we lost. Something.
I remember the surveyors. Nice young men, and they took the top of our field.
We were paid, and we were angry, and we were both for about a year.
Now my grandson can be in the capital by dinner. Ask me if I am still angry.
